section: Folk culture of Andhra - Burrakatha, Harikatha, Veedhi Natakam, Oggu Katha, Tolu Bommalata
subsections: Folk narrative forms - earlier names, performing community, instruments
Folk performance forms - home state, origin period, patrons
Burrakatha - troupe roles, famous troupes, political use

accepted.s:
Which of the following is associated with Burrakatha?
1. Jamukula Kathalu
2. Thandana Katha in Rayalaseema
3. Harikathalu
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Burrakatha is also known as Jamukula Kathalu and, in Rayalaseema, as Thandana Katha. Harikathalu is the other name of Harikatha.
accepted.tq: Separate closely related alternative names before selecting the combination.
accepted.sec: Folk narrative forms - earlier names, performing community, instruments

accepted.s: A traditional Burrakatha troupe generally consists of:
o: Two narrators and one actor playing a king
A main narrator and two Vantalu
A single narrator accompanied by a chorus
Three dancers accompanied by two drummers
accepted.x: The standard Burrakatha group has three members: the main narrator in the middle and two Vantalu who respond and comment.
accepted.tq: Use troupe composition to distinguish similar folk performance forms.
accepted.sec: Folk narrative forms - earlier names, performing community, instruments

accepted.s: Which one of the following sets contains instruments associated with Burrakatha?
accepted.x: Burrakatha uses the Gummata, Burra, Tambura and Ukki, along with the characteristic chorus phrase ‘Thandana Taana’.
accepted.tq: Identify the instrument set belonging to one specific form.
accepted.sec: Folk narrative forms - earlier names, performing community, instruments

accepted.s: The chorus phrase characteristically associated with Burrakatha is:
accepted.x: The Burrakatha performance includes the chorus phrase ‘Thandana Taana’.
accepted.tq: Test the distinctive verbal marker rather than the performer or instrument.
accepted.sec: Folk narrative forms - earlier names, performing community, instruments

accepted.s: With reference to Harikatha, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: It consists exclusively of puppet theatre.
It combines singing, acting and dancing by a single artist.
It is performed only by the Asadi sub-caste.
It is normally performed by a group of three narrators.
accepted.x: Harikatha is generally a solo performance in which one artist sings, acts and dances, usually for about three hours.
accepted.tq: Distinguish solo performance from group-based folk forms.
accepted.sec: Folk narrative forms - earlier names, performing community, instruments

accepted.s: The principal musical instrument specifically mentioned in connection with Harikatha is:
accepted.x: Harikatha performances use Chidatalu, or cymbals.
accepted.tq: Use the instrument-form association to eliminate neighbouring options.
accepted.sec: Folk narrative forms - earlier names, performing community, instruments

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Bhagavatulu:
1. They are mostly associated with the Yadava community.
2. Their performances centre on the Krishna Leelas.
3. They are particularly famous in Rayalaseema.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Bhagavatulu are mostly Yadavas, perform Krishna Leelas and are famous in Rayalaseema.
accepted.tq: Check whether all three linked identifiers belong to the same form.
accepted.sec: Folk narrative forms - earlier names, performing community, instruments

accepted.s: Which of the following best describes a performance of Bhagavatulu?
o: Three Pichukuntla performers sing Palnati Veeracharitra for fifteen nights.
A solo performer narrates for about three hours using only cymbals.
A group of shepherds sings rural ballads to a small drum.
The performers dance around a pillar bearing Sita-Rama-Lakshmana idols, using large bells, ankle bells and cymbals.
accepted.x: Bhagavatulu use Jeganta or large bells, ankle bells and cymbals, and dance around a pillar with Sita-Rama-Lakshmana idols.
accepted.tq: Match the performance format, instruments and ritual objects together.
accepted.sec: Folk narrative forms - earlier names, performing community, instruments

accepted.s: The story of Ellamma is traditionally associated with:
accepted.x: Asadi Katha is performed by the Asadi sub-caste of Madigas and narrates the story of Ellamma.
accepted.tq: Link the narrative subject with its performing community.
accepted.sec: Folk narrative forms - earlier names, performing community, instruments

accepted.s: Which pair is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Javiki and Chedika are the instruments of Asadi Katha. The other pairs assign instruments of different forms incorrectly.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure instrument-community association.
accepted.sec: Folk narrative forms - earlier names, performing community, instruments

accepted.s: Pichukuntla Katha is performed by:
o: A troupe of three from the Pichukuntla community
accepted.x: Pichukuntla Katha is performed by a troupe of three belonging to the Pichukuntla community.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the performing community from other narrative traditions.
accepted.sec: Folk narrative forms - earlier names, performing community, instruments

accepted.s: Which work is sung by the performers of Pichukuntla Katha?
o: Sugreeva Vijayam of Kandukuri Rudra Kavi
accepted.x: Pichukuntla performers sing Srinatha’s Palnati Veeracharitra, traditionally over fifteen nights.
accepted.tq: Use the author-work association to identify the folk form.
accepted.sec: Folk narrative forms - earlier names, performing community, instruments

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Pichukuntla Katha — turban, sword and shield
Harikatha — dance round a pillar with Sita-Rama-Lakshmana idols
accepted.x: Dance around a pillar with Sita-Rama-Lakshmana idols is associated with Bhagavatulu, not Harikatha.
accepted.tq: Find the performance detail transferred from one folk form to another.
accepted.sec: Folk narrative forms - earlier names, performing community, instruments

accepted.s: During the Vijayanagara period, the most popular entertainment of rural Andhra was:
accepted.x: Tholu Bommalata, the leather puppet show, was the most popular entertainment among the rural people of Andhra during the Vijayanagara period.
accepted.tq: Separate royal-court entertainment from rural popular entertainment.
accepted.sec: Folk performance forms - home state, origin period, patrons

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes Yakshaganam and Tholu Bommalata during the Vijayanagara period?
o: Yakshaganam was associated with royal courts and elites, whereas Tholu Bommalata was popular in rural Andhra.
Tholu Bommalata was confined to royal courts, whereas Yakshaganam was performed only in villages.
Both were exclusively temple rituals performed by the Veeramushti community.
Both were solo narrative performances using only cymbals.
accepted.x: Yakshaganam entertained royal courts and elites, while the leather puppet show was especially popular in rural Andhra.
accepted.tq: Read the comparison in both directions and reject the reversed relationship.
accepted.sec: Folk performance forms - home state, origin period, patrons

accepted.s: Late Vijayanagara patronage contributed to the development of:
o: Oggu Katha and Chindu Bhagavatam only
accepted.x: Late Vijayanagara patronage encouraged the development of Yakshaganas and Vachana, a prose-drama style.
accepted.tq: Identify the cultural forms linked to a particular period of patronage.
accepted.sec: Folk performance forms - home state, origin period, patrons

accepted.s: The Vipra-Vinodins of the late Vijayanagara period were:
o: Leather puppeteers performing in rural markets
Brahmin jugglers and actors performing for Brahmin households
Temple dancers attached to Shiva shrines
accepted.x: Vipra-Vinodins were Brahmin jugglers and actors who performed for Brahmin households.
accepted.tq: Use the occupation and patron group together to identify the term.
accepted.sec: Folk performance forms - home state, origin period, patrons

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the Qutb Shahi period?
accepted.x: Koravanji is described as an ancient precursor of Yakshagana in the context of the Qutb Shahi period.
accepted.tq: Match the historical-period association with the correct cultural form.
accepted.sec: Folk performance forms - home state, origin period, patrons

accepted.s: Who wrote Sugreeva Vijayam, regarded as the first published Yakshaganam in Telugu?
accepted.x: Sugreeva Vijayam, considered the first published Yakshaganam in Telugu, was written by Kandukuri Rudra Kavi.
accepted.tq: Apply the author-work trap common in history questions.
accepted.sec: Folk performance forms - home state, origin period, patrons

accepted.s: Which of the following were performed across the countryside during the Qutb Shahi period?
accepted.x: Bhagavata stories and Parijatam were performed across the countryside during the Qutb Shahi period.
accepted.tq: Identify the pair belonging to the stated historical setting.
accepted.sec: Folk performance forms - home state, origin period, patrons

accepted.s: Which work records the staging of Harikathas, Natakams and Purana Kalakshepams at temple festivals during the Eastern Chalukya period?
accepted.x: Someshwara’s Abhilashitartha Chintamani, also known as Manasollasa, records these performances at temple festivals.
accepted.tq: Use the text-title and patron-author association carefully.
accepted.sec: Folk performance forms - home state, origin period, patrons

accepted.s: Burrakatha is traditionally associated with which place as its birthplace?
accepted.x: Guntur is identified as the birthplace of Burrakatha. It is a folk form associated with Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
accepted.tq: Distinguish birthplace from the wider geographical area of practice.
accepted.sec: Folk performance forms - home state, origin period, patrons

accepted.s: Veedhi Bhagavatam literally refers to:
o: A Shaiva dance in Shiva temples
A form of leather puppet theatre
Bhagavatam performed only in royal courts
accepted.x: Veedhi Bhagavatam means ‘Bhagavatam in the street’ and denotes street theatre.
accepted.tq: Use the literal meaning to identify the cultural form.
accepted.sec: Folk performance forms - home state, origin period, patrons

accepted.s: Which statement about the Yakshaganam of Andhra is correct?
o: It is performed only in Sanskrit without costumes.
It is a shepherd ballad accompanied by the Oggu drum.
It is a solo performance centred exclusively on philosophy.
It is performed in Telugu with elaborate costumes and epic or Puranic stories.
accepted.x: Andhra Yakshaganam is performed in Telugu, uses elaborate costumes and presents epic or Puranic stories.
accepted.tq: Combine language, costume and subject matter to identify the form.
accepted.sec: Folk performance forms - home state, origin period, patrons

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT a component fused by Adibhatla Narayana Dasu into Harikatha?
accepted.x: Narayana Dasu fused music, story-telling, dance, philosophy and literature into Harikatha. Leather puppetry is associated with Tholu Bommalata.
accepted.tq: Find the unrelated art form among the components of a composite performance.
accepted.sec: Harikatha - founder and exponents

accepted.s: Adibhatla Narayana Dasu was a:
o: Brahmin juggler of the Vipra-Vinodin group
accepted.x: Adibhatla Narayana Dasu was a multilingual scholar who developed Harikatha as a composite performance tradition.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the performer’s scholarly identity from community-based folk performers.
accepted.sec: Harikatha - founder and exponents

accepted.s: Which of the following is a kavya written by Adibhatla Narayana Dasu?
accepted.x: Jagajyothi and Navarasa Tarangini are among the kavyas of Adibhatla Narayana Dasu. The other works belong to Burrakatha-related literature.
accepted.tq: Use genre and authorship to separate literary works from political Burrakathas.
accepted.sec: Harikatha - founder and exponents

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with Adibhatla Narayana Dasu?
o: Navarasa Tarangini — historical ballad on the Bobbili War
accepted.x: Na Yeruka is the autobiography of Adibhatla Narayana Dasu. Sri Krishna Kathamrutam is his Sanskrit Harikatha, while the other descriptions are incorrect.
accepted.tq: Separate literary genres—autobiography, Harikatha and political ballad.
accepted.sec: Harikatha - founder and exponents

accepted.s: Which statement regarding Harikatha is correct?
o: It has deep roots in Vizianagaram.
It is another name for Veedhi Bhagavatam.
It originated exclusively among the Pichukuntla community.
It is confined to Rayalaseema and absent from Vizianagaram.
accepted.x: Harikatha has deep roots in Vizianagaram, a region also associated with Adibhatla Narayana Dasu.
accepted.tq: Test the regional association without confusing it with the home region of another form.
accepted.sec: Harikatha - founder and exponents

accepted.s: In a Burrakatha troupe, the main narrator generally:
o: Dances around a pillar with idols
Stands in the middle and plays the burra
Acts as one of the two Vantalu and never narrates
Plays only the cymbals from outside the performing area
accepted.x: The main narrator stands in the middle, plays the burra and leads the performance; the two Vantalu respond and comment.
accepted.tq: Use stage position and role to distinguish the central performer from supporting members.
accepted.sec: Burrakatha - troupe roles, famous troupes, political use

accepted.s: The two Vantalu in Burrakatha primarily:
o: Operate leather puppets behind a screen
Respond to and comment on the main narrator’s presentation
Perform the entire narrative without the main narrator
accepted.x: The two Vantalu support the main narrator by responding and commenting during the performance.
accepted.tq: Test functional roles within a troupe rather than names of performers.
accepted.sec: Burrakatha - troupe roles, famous troupes, political use

accepted.s: Burrakatha traditionally evokes which rasas?
accepted.x: Burrakatha evokes heroic and tragic rasas through its narrative and performance style.
accepted.tq: Associate the emotional effect with the correct narrative form.
accepted.sec: Burrakatha - troupe roles, famous troupes, political use

accepted.s: Sheikh Nazar, regarded as the Pitamaha of Burrakatha, was born on:
accepted.x: Sheikh Nazar, the Pitamaha of Burrakatha, was born on 5 February 1920 at Pannekallu in Guntur.
accepted.tq: Read the exact date rather than relying on a familiar national date.
accepted.sec: Burrakatha - troupe roles, famous troupes, political use

accepted.s: Sheikh Nazar was born at:
o: A village in Telangana associated with Oggu Katha
accepted.x: Sheikh Nazar was born at Pannekallu in Guntur. Ajjada village in Vizianagaram district is associated with Adibhatla Narayana Dasu.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the birthplaces of two major folk-art exponents.
accepted.sec: Burrakatha - troupe roles, famous troupes, political use

accepted.s: Which pair of works is associated with Sheikh Nazar?
accepted.x: Sheikh Nazar’s works include Palnati Yuddham and Bengal Karuvu. The other pairs include works of Sunkara Satyanarayana or Adibhatla Narayana Dasu.
accepted.tq: Use the author-work association and reject mixed-author options.
accepted.sec: Burrakatha - troupe roles, famous troupes, political use

accepted.s: Who among the following is identified as a researcher associated with Burrakatha?
accepted.x: Dr. Tangirala Subbarao is identified as a researcher of Burrakatha. The other persons are associated with Yakshaganam, Manasollasa or Harikatha.
accepted.tq: Distinguish researcher, performer and author roles.
accepted.sec: Burrakatha - troupe roles, famous troupes, political use

accepted.s: Which of the following names is included among the popularisers of Burrakatha?
accepted.x: Nazar, the Nittala Brothers and Bhadrakali are listed among the popularisers of Burrakatha.
accepted.tq: Identify the popularising group from among authors of related works.
accepted.sec: Burrakatha - troupe roles, famous troupes, political use

accepted.s: Which of the following Burrakathas is associated with Sunkara Satyanarayana?
accepted.x: Sunkara Satyanarayana wrote or performed Burrakathas such as Kashtajeevi, Raithu Vijayam, Stalin, Alluri Sitaramaraju and Veeresalingam.
accepted.tq: Match the political Burrakatha title with its associated creator.
accepted.sec: Burrakatha - troupe roles, famous troupes, political use

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT associated with Sunkara Satyanarayana’s Burrakatha repertoire?
accepted.x: Bengal Karuvu is associated with Sheikh Nazar. Sunkara Satyanarayana’s listed works include Raithu Vijayam, Alluri Sitaramaraju and Veeresalingam.
accepted.tq: Find the work belonging to the neighbouring but different performer.
accepted.sec: Burrakatha - troupe roles, famous troupes, political use

accepted.s: The Praja Natya Mandali used folk plays primarily to spread:
accepted.x: The Praja Natya Mandali used folk plays to communicate socialist and communist ideals.
accepted.tq: Identify the stated political purpose of a cultural organisation.
accepted.sec: Burrakatha - troupe roles, famous troupes, political use

accepted.s: Mabhoomi, a hit folk play of the Praja Natya Mandali, was associated with:
o: Sunkara Satyanarayana and Vasireddy Bhaskara Rao
Sheikh Nazar and Dr. Tangirala Subbarao
Adibhatla Narayana Dasu and Kandukuri Rudra Kavi
accepted.x: Mabhoomi was associated with Sunkara Satyanarayana and Vasireddy Bhaskara Rao.
accepted.tq: Match a famous political performance with its two associated creators.
accepted.sec: Burrakatha - troupe roles, famous troupes, political use

accepted.s: The political and social utility of Burrakatha lay chiefly in the fact that its narrators:
o: Performed only before educated urban elites
Restricted their narratives to temple festivals
Avoided contemporary political and social issues
Carried news, reformist ideas and nationalist messages to unlettered villages
accepted.x: Burrakatha narrators communicated news, reform and nationalist messages to unlettered rural populations.
accepted.tq: Apply the communication function of a folk form to a social situation.
accepted.sec: Burrakatha - troupe roles, famous troupes, political use

accepted.s: Which pair of books and years is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Telugulo Burrakathalu was published in 1986, while Burrakathalu was published in 1988.
accepted.tq: Match each title with its distinct publication year instead of reversing the pair.
accepted.sec: Burrakatha - troupe roles, famous troupes, political use

accepted.s: Who is associated with the book Telugulo Burrakathalu?
accepted.x: K.H. Lakshman Rao is associated with Telugulo Burrakathalu, published in 1986.
accepted.tq: Use title-author association to distinguish two Burrakatha books.
accepted.sec: Burrakatha - troupe roles, famous troupes, political use

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Burrakathalu was associated with Kuvvada Vijayakumar and was published in 1988.
accepted.tq: Check both the author and year before accepting a bibliographic match.
accepted.sec: Burrakatha - troupe roles, famous troupes, political use

accepted.s: The historical ballads of Burrakatha draw upon events such as the:
accepted.x: Burrakatha historical ballads draw upon events such as the Bobbili War of 1757, in which Vijayarama Raju of Vizianagaram sought French assistance.
accepted.tq: Use the event-year pairing and associated political actors together.
accepted.sec: Burrakatha - troupe roles, famous troupes, political use

accepted.s: In the context of the Bobbili War of 1757, Vijayarama Raju of Vizianagaram took the help of the:
accepted.x: Vijayarama Raju of Vizianagaram took French assistance in the Bobbili War of 1757; Bussy is associated with this French support.
accepted.tq: Identify the foreign ally rather than the regional ruler involved.
accepted.sec: Burrakatha - troupe roles, famous troupes, political use

accepted.s: Oggu Katha is best described as:
o: A solo Andhra performance combining philosophy and literature with cymbals
A Shaiva temple dance performed by the Veeramushti community
A Telangana ballad form voicing rural life and struggle, sung by the Golla/Kuruma community to a small oggu drum
A leather puppet show popular in rural Andhra under Vijayanagara
accepted.x: Oggu Katha is a Telangana ballad tradition of rural life and struggle, performed by the Golla/Kuruma shepherd community with a small oggu drum.
accepted.tq: Combine region, community, subject and instrument to identify the form.
accepted.sec: Folk narrative forms - earlier names, performing community, instruments

accepted.s: Chindu Bhagavatam is associated with:
o: The Veeramushti community in Shiva temples
Chindu performers, a sub-group of Madigas, in Telangana
Brahmin jugglers of the Vijayanagara period
accepted.x: Chindu Bhagavatam is a Telangana dance-drama performed by Chindus, a Madiga sub-group.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the performer community and region from similar traditions.
accepted.sec: Folk narrative forms - earlier names, performing community, instruments

accepted.s: Veeranatyam is a Shaiva ritual dance associated with:
o: The Asadi sub-caste of Madigas narrating Ellamma’s story
The Veeramushti community in Shiva temples
The Golla/Kuruma community with the oggu drum
The Pichukuntla community in village streets
accepted.x: Veeranatyam is the Shaiva ritual dance of Veerabhadra, performed in Shiva temples by the Veeramushti community.
accepted.tq: Use deity, ritual setting and community as a three-part identifier.
accepted.sec: Folk narrative forms - earlier names, performing community, instruments
